Thanks Ellen — sketching the operational requirements below and attaching the initial manifest and signer roster for review. Quick summary (see attachments):

Must-have manifest fields:
- image_build_id (semantic)
- sha256(image) and sha256(manifest)
- signing_key_id and certificate chain fingerprint
- build_artifacts: [list of bundles + checksums]
- provenance_url (if applicable)

Signer quorum and succession:
- Primary quorum: 3 signers (Operator A, Security B, Custodian C).
- If a primary signer is unavailable at arrival, succession rule: allow 1 substitute from the operator roster + notarized on-site statement; must be recorded and hashed into the acceptance log.

On-site acceptance (gating checklist):
1) Manifest hash matches delivered image (operator runs local sha256).
2) Signatures verify against roster pubkeys.
3) Operator performs isolated boot smoke test (10 min) — logs collected to sealed USB.
4) If any mismatch, escalate to Redwood ops, revert to fallback image (signed fallback manifest) and document courier chain-of-custody.

Attachments included: manifest-v3.json, signer_roster.csv, staged-rollout-timeline.xlsx

Next steps:
- Ben, can you confirm the fallback manifest location and how we handle an emergency signed delta?
- Naomi, can you prepare the acceptance log template we want the site to return (we'll hash it into the ledger)?

I can join a quick sync with DeltaCloud and Munson later this week if helpful.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Manager, Enterprise Deployments
Redwood Inference

- Fallback manifest: stored in the signed-bundles S3 (vaulted path) and referenced by manifest-v3 as fallback_build_id. I will produce a short signed_delta artifact if we need a small security patch; process is: produce signed_delta -> notarize -> courier-only delta package.

- Emergency measure: if site refuses, we instruct courier to hold in quarantine and collect the sealed evidence package. We will open SUP-3421 for any on-site disputes and kick a remote attestation session.

- On the smoke test: keep the window at 10 minutes, but also capture serial console output (first 300 lines) and a CRC of the acceptance log. That gives us deterministic artifacts for forensics.
